claim: Live-imaging techniques for the adult midgut of Drosophila melanogaster have been limited to imaging sessions of <16 hours.
source: However, these organ culture techniques have been limited to imaging sessions of <16 hours, an interval too short to track dynamic processes such as damage responses and regeneration, which can unfold over several days.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing techniques in the abstract, supported by citations to previous work in the introduction.

claim: An organ explant culture protocol was developed capable of sustaining midguts ex vivo for up to 3 days.
source: Therefore, we developed an organ explant culture protocol capable of sustaining midguts ex vivo for up to 3 days.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The extended culture was made possible by formulating a culture medium with an increased Na+/K+ ratio and trehalose concentration.
source: This was made possible by the formulation of a culture medium specifically designed for adult Drosophila tissues with an increased Na+/K+ ratio and trehalose concentration, and by placing midguts at an air-liquid interface for enhanced oxygenation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 2A and Table 1.

claim: Placing midguts at an air-liquid interface enhances oxygenation and enables extended culture.
source: This was made possible by the formulation of a culture medium specifically designed for adult Drosophila tissues with an increased Na+/K+ ratio and trehalose concentration, and by placing midguts at an air-liquid interface for enhanced oxygenation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a key design element and discussed in the results section.

claim: Midgut progenitor cells can respond to gut epithelial damage ex vivo by proliferating and differentiating to replace lost cells.
source: We show that midgut progenitor cells can respond to gut epithelial damage ex vivo, proliferating and differentiating to replace lost cells, but are quiescent in healthy intestines.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated with data in Figure 3.

claim: Progenitor cells are quiescent in healthy intestines ex vivo.
source: We show that midgut progenitor cells can respond to gut epithelial damage ex vivo, proliferating and differentiating to replace lost cells, but are quiescent in healthy intestines.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated with data in Figure 3A and Figure 3D, F, G.

claim: Ex vivo gene induction using RasG12V promotes stem cell proliferation.
source: Using ex vivo gene induction to promote stem cell proliferation using RasG12V or string and Cyclin E overexpression, we demonstrate that progenitor cell lineages can be traced through multiple cell divisions using live imaging.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated with data in Figure 4B.

claim: Ex vivo gene induction using string and Cyclin E overexpression promotes stem cell proliferation.
source: Using ex vivo gene induction to promote stem cell proliferation using RasG12V or string and Cyclin E overexpression, we demonstrate that progenitor cell lineages can be traced through multiple cell divisions using live imaging.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated with data in Figure 4C.

claim: Progenitor cell lineages can be traced through multiple cell divisions using live imaging.
source: Using ex vivo gene induction to promote stem cell proliferation using RasG12V or string and Cyclin E overexpression, we demonstrate that progenitor cell lineages can be traced through multiple cell divisions using live imaging.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated with data in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: The culture set-up is useful for imaging adult renal tubules for up to 3 days.
source: We show that the same culture set-up is useful for imaging adult renal tubules and ovaries for up to 3 days and hearts for up to 10 days.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated with data in Figure 8A-B.

claim: The culture set-up is useful for imaging ovaries for up to 3 days.
source: We show that the same culture set-up is useful for imaging adult renal tubules and ovaries for up to 3 days and hearts for up to 10 days.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated with data in Figure 8C.

claim: The culture set-up is useful for imaging hearts for up to 10 days.
source: We show that the same culture set-up is useful for imaging adult renal tubules and ovaries for up to 3 days and hearts for up to 10 days.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated with Video 3.

claim: Intestinal stem cells (ISCs) in the adult Drosophila midgut can interpret signals from their surrounding environment such as cytokines released by neighboring damaged enterocytes.
source: The adult Drosophila melanogaster midgut is a prime example of this as its population of intestinal stem cells (ISCs) are able to interpret signals from their surrounding environment such as cytokines released by neighboring damaged enterocytes (EC) (Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006; Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Jiang et al., 2009; Beebe et al., 2010; Patel et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Normally quiescent stem cells rapidly respond to tissue needs by proliferating and stimulating differentiation of their progeny to replace lost cells.
source: When this interaction occurs, normally quiescent stem cells rapidly respond to the needs of the tissue, proliferating and stimulating the differentiation of their progeny to replace lost cells, thus repairing the damaged epithelium (Jiang et al., 2009; Patel et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Current live-imaging protocols for the adult Drosophila midgut are limited to 16 hr imaging sessions.
source: Current live-imaging protocols for the adult Drosophila midgut are limited to 16 hr imaging sessions (Deng et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2017; He et al., 2018; Martin et al., 2018; Hu and Jasper, 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The dissection technique is a key parameter in extending the viability of explanted midguts.
source: We found that the dissection technique is a key parameter in extending the viability of explanted midguts.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on experimental observations.

claim: Stress introduced during dissection results in structural damage which leads to breaks of the epithelium during prolonged culture.
source: Indeed, any stress (e.g. pulling and thus stretching the gut, pinching, etc...) introduced during dissection results in structural damage which lead to breaks of the epithelium during prolonged culture.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on experimental observations.

claim: Proper oxygenation is essential for the long-term survival of explanted midguts.
source: This is a key design element of the setup, as proper oxygenation was found to be essential for the long-term survival of explanted midguts (data not shown), similarly to what had been previously observed for the culture of wing imaginal discs (Strassburger et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation to previous work on imaginal discs.

claim: During dissection the trachea surrounding the intestine are severed and can no longer oxygenate the intestinal epithelium.
source: Moreover, during dissection the trachea surrounding the intestine are severed and can no longer oxygenate the intestinal epithelium.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a logical consequence of the dissection procedure.

claim: Raising the concentration of trehalose and mimicking the Na+/K+ ratio of adult hemolymph is sufficient to significantly reduce cell death after 24 hr of culture.
source: We found that raising the concentration of trehalose, which is found at high levels in Drosophila circulation (Pasco and Léopold, 2012; Dus et al., 2013; Park et al., 2014; Tennessen et al., 2014; Matsushita and Nishimura, 2014), and mimicking the Na+/K+ ratio of adult hemolymph (Singleton and Woodruff, 1994; Naikkhwah and O'Donnell, 2014; MacMillan et al., 2015b; MacMillan et al., 2015a; Olsson et al., 2016) is sufficient to significantly reduce cell death after 24 hr of culture.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2A and citations to previous work on hemolymph composition.

claim: Trehalose is found at high levels in Drosophila circulation.
source: We found that raising the concentration of trehalose, which is found at high levels in Drosophila circulation (Pasco and Léopold, 2012; Dus et al., 2013; Park et al., 2014; Tennessen et al., 2014; Matsushita and Nishimura, 2014), and mimicking the Na+/K+ ratio of adult hemolymph (Singleton and Woodruff, 1994; Naikkhwah and O'Donnell, 2014; MacMillan et al., 2015b; MacMillan et al., 2015a; Olsson et al., 2016) is sufficient to significantly reduce cell death after 24 hr of culture.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Supplementing the culture medium with 10% fetal bovine serum did not have a significant beneficial effect on the midgut epithelium.
source: Our tests showed that supplementing the culture medium with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) did not have a significant beneficial effect on the midgut epithelium (Figure 2A), but we did notice that FBS addition resulted in the visceral muscle remaining intact and capable of peristalsis for longer (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: FBS addition resulted in the visceral muscle remaining intact and capable of peristalsis for longer.
source: Our tests showed that supplementing the culture medium with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) did not have a significant beneficial effect on the midgut epithelium (Figure 2A), but we did notice that FBS addition resulted in the visceral muscle remaining intact and capable of peristalsis for longer (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on experimental observations.

claim: Co-culturing explanted midguts with ovaries and abdomens lined with fat body can decrease cell death ex vivo.
source: Not surprisingly (Davis and Shearn, 1977; Britton and Edgar, 1998), co-culturing explanted midguts with ovaries and abdomens lined with fat body (adipocytes) could also decrease cell death ex vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2A and citations to previous work.

claim: Midguts cultured in 100% fly extract prepared using modified Schneider's medium had greatly reduced rates of cell death over time.
source: Indeed, midguts cultured in 100% fly extract prepared using modified Schneider's medium had greatly reduced rates of cell death over time (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: The calcium blocker isradipine was added to the medium to reduce peristaltic movements, improving midgut survival and imaging.
source: The calcium blocker isradipine was also added to the medium to reduce peristaltic movements, improving midgut survival and imaging.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on experimental observations.

claim: The effect of isradipine appeared to wear off after 48–72 hr, at which point the visceral muscle resumed regular peristalsis.
source: This drug did not have a noticeable long-term effect on visceral muscle viability. Indeed, its effect appeared to wear off after 48–72 hr, at which point the visceral muscle resumed regular peristalsis (Video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Video 1.

claim: N-acetyl cysteine and sodium citrate were added as antioxidant agents to reduce phototoxicity.
source: Lastly, as we designed the medium for the purpose of extended live-imaging, we also added N-acetyl cysteine and sodium citrate as antioxidant agents to reduce phototoxicity (Icha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation to previous work on phototoxicity.

claim: N-acetyl cysteine is an antioxidant widely used in cell culture.
source: The former is an antioxidant widely used in cell culture (Ezeriņa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Citrate is known to have antioxidant properties.
source: Citrate is also known to have antioxidant properties (Wu et al., 2019) and to be present in Drosophila hemolymph at detectable levels (Echalier et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Citrate is present in Drosophila hemolymph at detectable levels.
source: Citrate is also known to have antioxidant properties (Wu et al., 2019) and to be present in Drosophila hemolymph at detectable levels (Echalier et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Esg-expressing progenitor cells (ISCs and EBs) were observed to be quiescent in explanted healthy guts.
source: When imaging explanted adult Drosophila midguts we observed esg-expressing progenitor cells (ISCs and EBS) to be quiescent (Figure 3A and Figure 2—video 1, Figure 3—video 1, Figure 3—video 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3A and associated videos.

claim: Progenitor cells in explanted healthy guts did not show major changes in their GFP levels, indicative of continuous esg expression.
source: Progenitor cells in explanted healthy guts did not show major changes in their GFP levels, indicative of continuous esg expression, nor in their nuclear size (Figure 3D, F and G and Figure 3—video 4), which indicates that DNA content remains constant.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3D, F, and G.

claim: Progenitor cells in explanted healthy guts did not show major changes in their nuclear size, which indicates that DNA content remains constant.
source: Progenitor cells in explanted healthy guts did not show major changes in their GFP levels, indicative of continuous esg expression, nor in their nuclear size (Figure 3D, F and G and Figure 3—video 4), which indicates that DNA content remains constant.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3D, F, and G.

claim: GFP-labeled progenitor cells did not divide in healthy explanted intestines.
source: Via cell tracking we also observed that GFP-labeled progenitor cells did not divide in healthy explanted intestines (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: In healthy explanted intestines, cell death or enterocyte (EC) extrusion events were not observed until after 48–72 hr of culture.
source: It is important to note that in said healthy intestines we did not observe cell death or enterocyte (EC) extrusion events until after 48–72 hr of culture.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on experimental observations.

claim: Healthy enterocytes are known to suppress ISC proliferation.
source: As healthy enterocytes are known to suppress ISC proliferation (Liang et al., 2017), this may explain the lack of cell division in our explants.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The suppression of peristaltic movements by isradipine may prevent EC loss by reducing mechanical tissue stress.
source: The suppression of peristaltic movements by isradipine may also prevent EC loss by reducing mechanical tissue stress (Li et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a hypothesis supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: ISC proliferation events could be detected in SDS-damaged intestines.
source: ISC proliferation events could also be detected (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3C.

claim: ISC mitoses could generally be observed only in cases where tissue damage was extensive.
source: However, ISC mitoses could generally be observed only in cases where tissue damage was extensive, as evidenced by the appearance of pyknotic or fragmented nuclei and the extrusion of multiple (>3) contiguous ECs.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on experimental observations.

claim: Many progenitor cells could be observed growing in nuclear size while simultaneously losing GFP expression, indicative of differentiation events towards the EC identity.
source: In addition to ISC divisions, many progenitor cells could be observed growing in nuclear size while simultaneously losing GFP expression (Figure 3B and E–G and Figure 3—video 3, Figure 3—video 4) indicative of differentiation events towards the EC identity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3B, E-G and associated videos.

claim: Differentiating progenitor cells could be seen replacing dying enterocytes.
source: Indeed, differentiating progenitor cells could be seen replacing dying enterocytes (Figure 3—video 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Figure 3—video 3.

claim: After SDS feeding, several esg+ cells with larger nuclei were observed.
source: After SDS feeding, we observed several esg + cells with larger nuclei (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: At later time-points after SDS treatment, many differentiating cells with large nuclei and low GFP expression were present.
source: At later time-points many differentiating cells with large nuclei and low GFP expression were also present, similarl to what was observed ex vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Proliferative cells could be found almost exclusively at 48 hr after the end of the SDS treatment.
source: Moreover, similarly to explanted midguts, proliferative cells could be found almost exclusively at 48 hr after the end of the SDS treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Progenitor cells could be observed both dividing and differentiating in response to wounding with a tungsten needle.
source: Similarly to the SDS damage protocol, we were able to record progenitor cells both dividing and differentiating (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C and Figure 3—video 5).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C and Figure 3—video 5.

claim: Wounding stimulated the robust expression of the cytokine Unpaired 3 (Upd3).
source: Moreover, wounding stimulated the robust expression of the cytokine Unpaired 3 (Upd3), whose function in midgut damage response is well documented (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D, E and Figure 3—video 6; Figure 3—video 7; Jiang et al., 2009; Patel et al., 2015; Buchon et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D, E and associated videos, as well as citations to previous work.

claim: Both ISCs and EBs are quiescent in undamaged intestines.
source: All in all, our observations suggest that both ISCs and EBs are quiescent in undamaged intestines.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: Previous studies showed varying rates of ISC proliferation in healthy midguts in vivo.
source: While previous studies did show varying rates of ISC proliferation in healthy midguts in vivo (Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006; Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Jiang et al., 2009; Reiff et al., 2019; de Navascués et al., 2012), this may be attributed to cell death (Liang et al., 2017) as well as the passage of food through the intestinal lumen (Li et al., 2018), both of which do not occur in our midgut cultures until later time-points (i.e. after 48–72 hr).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Several previous studies used lineage-tracing tools requiring a 37 °C heat shock for their activation, a treatment known to induce ISC proliferation.
source: Moreover, several previous studies used lineage-tracing tools requiring a 37 °C heat shock for their activation, a treatment known to induce ISC proliferation (Beebe et al., 2010; de Navascués et al., 2012; Lin et al., 2008; Shaw et al., 2010; Strand and Micchelli, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: In the presence of tissue damage, progenitor cells could be robustly activated in explanted intestines.
source: Indeed, in the presence of tissue damage, progenitor cells could be robustly activated in explanted intestines, indicating that both ISCs and EBs are capable of responding to their environment after organ explant.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on experimental observations.

claim: The Delta/Notch signaling that occurs between ISCs and adjacent EBs is a key pathway necessary for progenitor cell differentiation.
source: A key pathway necessary for progenitor cell differentiation is the Delta/Notch signaling that occurs between ISCs and adjacent EBs (Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006; Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The depletion of Notch (N) by RNA interference (NRNAi) in esg+ cells has been shown to promote the formation of undifferentiated tumor-like masses in vivo.
source: The depletion of Notch (N) by RNA interference (NRNAi) in esg+ cells has been shown to promote the formation of undifferentiated tumor-like masses in vivo (Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006; Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Patel et al., 2015; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Tumor initiation by N-depleted ISCs requires proliferation induced by tissue stress.
source: Notably, tumor initiation by N-depleted ISCs requires proliferation induced by tissue stress (Patel et al., 2015; Apidianakis et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: When midguts from flies expressing NRNAi in progenitor cells for 24 h prior to dissection were cultured for 48 hr, tumorigenesis was not observed in the absence of tissue damage.
source: Consistent with this, when we explanted midguts from flies expressing NRNAi in progenitor cells for 24 h prior to dissection and cultured them for 48 hr, we did not observe tumorigenesis in the absence of tissue damage (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and Figure 3—video 8).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and Figure 3—video 8.

claim: When guts expressing NRNAi were accidentally damaged during dissection, esg+ cells started to proliferate.
source: However, when guts were accidentally damaged during dissection (Figure 3—figure supplement 3, yellow ellipses), esg+ cells started to proliferate (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B, yellow squares, and Figure 3—video 9).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B and Figure 3—video 9.

claim: Progenitor cells expressing NRNAi remained small and did not lose GFP expression, suggesting a block of differentiation ex vivo in response to Notch knock-down.
source: Notably, progenitor cells remained small and did not lose GFP expression (compare Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B as well as Figure 3—video 2 and Figure 3—video 9), suggesting a block of differentiation ex vivo in response to Notch knock-down.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B and Figure 3—video 9.

claim: EGFR-Ras-Erk signaling is activated upon gut tissue damage.
source: EGFR-Ras-Erk signaling is activated upon gut tissue damage, and this pathway is required for stem cell activation in the adult Drosophila intestine (Buchon et al., 2010; Biteau and Jasper, 2011; Jiang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: EGFR-Ras-Erk signaling is required for stem cell activation in the adult Drosophila intestine.
source: EGFR-Ras-Erk signaling is activated upon gut tissue damage, and this pathway is required for stem cell activation in the adult Drosophila intestine (Buchon et al., 2010; Biteau and Jasper, 2011; Jiang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Expression of a constitutively active form of Ras (RasG12V) strongly promotes stem cell proliferation in adult midguts.
source: Previous experiments showed that expression of a constitutively active form of Ras (RasG12V) strongly promotes stem cell proliferation in adult midguts (Jiang et al., 2011; Jin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: When RasG12V was induced in explanted midguts using the esgTS driver, progenitor cells started to rapidly proliferate.
source: When explanted midguts were shifted to the permissive temperature (29 °C) at the start of imaging, progenitor cells, marked by GFP co-expressed with RasG12V, started to rapidly proliferate (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4B.

claim: About 20% of progenitor cells tracked from the moment they expressed visible amounts of GFP till the end of the imaging session were seen proliferating after RasG12V expression.
source: About 20% of progenitor cells tracked from the moment they expressed visible amounts of GFP till the end of the imaging session, were seen proliferating (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4D.

claim: As GFP+ cells accumulated in the tissue after RasG12V expression, enterocytes were displaced and extruded from the epithelium.
source: As GFP+ cells accumulated in the tissue, enterocytes were displaced and extruded from the epithelium (Figure 4B, yellow arrowhead, and Figure 4—video 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4B and Figure 4—video 2.

claim: Some GFP+ progenitor cells expressing RasG12V did not proliferate, but their nuclei rapidly grew in size, which aligns with the previously reported role of EGFR signaling in promoting EB growth.
source: Interestingly, some GFP+ progenitor cells did not proliferate, but their nuclei rapidly grew in size, which aligns with the previously reported role of EGFR signaling in promoting EB growth (Jiang et al., 2011; Xiang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Rapidly growing progenitors expressing RasG12V also lost GFP expression during the course of imaging, which suggests their differentiation towards the EC lineage.
source: Moreover, these rapidly growing progenitors also lost GFP expression during the course of imaging, which suggests their differentiation towards the EC lineage.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on experimental observations.

claim: The extended live-imaging that the protocol allows permitted following cells through multiple rounds of mitosis.
source: The extended live-imaging that our protocol allows also permitted us to follow cells through multiple rounds of mitosis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on experimental observations.

claim: Using manual 3-dimensional (3D) cell tracking, the lineages of 17 dividing cells that expressed RasG12V were reconstructed.
source: Using manual 3-dimensional (3D) cell tracking, we reconstructed the lineages of 17 dividing cells that expressed RasG12V (see Figure 5 and Figure 5—video 1 for an example).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 5 and Figure 5—video 1.

claim: ISCs are the only cell type in the Drosophila intestine that normally divide multiple times.
source: As ISCs are the only cell type in the Drosophila intestine that normally divide multiple times (Ohlstein and Spradling, 2006; Micchelli and Perrimon, 2006; Chen et al., 2018), the founding cells in these lineages were most likely ISCs.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: A recent work suggested that RasG12V can push a small number of EBs to de-differentiate to an ISC state.
source: However, a recent work suggested that RasG12V can push a small number of EBs to de-differentiate to an ISC state (Tian et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation to recent work.

claim: The duration of progenitors' cell cycle in RasG12V-expressing lineages was directly measured to be 8±2.76 hr.
source: We directly measured the duration of progenitors' cell cycle in these lineages to be 8±2.76 hr (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4F.

claim: Of 17 RasG12V-expressing ISC lineages characterized, one had divisions where both daughter cells from the first recorded division were seen dividing further.
source: Interestingly, of 17 RasG12V-expressing ISC lineages characterized, one had divisions where both daughter cells from the first recorded division were seen dividing further (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4E.

claim: After being generated from an ISC division, enteroendocrine (EE) progenitors are known to divide once to give rise to two mature EEs.
source: For example, after being generated from an ISC division, enteroendocrine (EE) progenitors are also known to divide once to give rise to two mature EEs (Chen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Co-expression of string (stg) and Cyclin E (CycE) is sufficient to strongly induce ISC proliferation.
source: The combined expression of these two gene products is sufficient to strongly induce ISC proliferation (Kohlmaier et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Stg and CycE have been shown to promote EB mitoses, although much less strongly than in ISCs.
source: Notably, Stg and CycE have also been shown to promote EB mitoses (Kohlmaier et al., 2015), although much less strongly than in ISCs.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The fraction of progenitor cells that divided in response to stg and CycE co-expression (~25%) was not significantly different from that observed after forced expression of RasG12V.
source: The fraction of progenitor cells that divided in response to stg and CycE co-expression (~25%; Figure 4D) was not significantly different from that observed after forced expression of RasG12V, suggesting that all receptive progenitors are activated in both cases.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4D.

claim: Co-dividing siblings appeared in 6 of 12 ISC lineages that overexpressed stg and CycE.
source: However, co-dividing siblings appeared in 6 of 12 ISC lineages that overexpressed stg and CycE (Figure 4E), a significantly higher frequency to the 1 of 17 observed after RasG12V overexpression (p=0.0106, Fisher's exact test).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4E and statistical analysis.

claim: No significant difference in cell cycle duration was detected in progenitors' cell cycles driven by stg and CycE (9.4±4.6 hr) and cell cycles driven by RasG12V (8±2.76 hr).
source: We detected no significant difference in cell cycle duration in progenitors' cell cycles driven by stg and CycE (9.4±4.6 hr) and cell cycles driven by RasG12V (8±2.76 hr; Figure 4F), suggesting that their differing abilities to produce co-dividing sibling cells may reflect different effects on the differentiation process.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4F.

claim: Eight divisions yielded co-dividing siblings.
source: Combining all the lineages described above, we were able to identify eight divisions that yielded co-dividing siblings (see Figure 6A–B and Figure 5—video 1 for an example).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6A-B and Figure 5—video 1.

claim: For seven co-dividing sibling pairs, sibling cells divided within 2 hr of each other.
source: For seven of these, sibling cells divided within 2 hr of each other, while for one pair the interval was 5 hr.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on experimental observations.

claim: 17 sibling pairs were classified as non-co-dividing.
source: Following this definition, we classified 17 sibling pairs as non-co-dividing (see Figure 6D–F and Figure 6—video 2 for an example), 9 from RasG12V- and 8 from stg and CycE-expressing guts.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6D-F and Figure 6—video 2.

claim: For 8 of 17 non-co-dividing pairs, the non-dividing cells displayed increases in nuclear size over time and lost GFP expression, which is indicative of differentiation towards the EC cell fate.
source: Interestingly, for 8 of these 17 pairs, the non-dividing cells displayed increases in nuclear size over time, and also lost GFP expression, which is indicative of differentiation towards the EC cell fate (Figure 6C and G–H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6C and G-H.

claim: Co-dividing siblings increased their nuclear size before dividing further, but maintained GFP expression.
source: This behavior was not observed for co-dividing siblings, where both cells increased their nuclear size before dividing further, but maintained GFP expression (Figure 6A and E–F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6A and E-F.

claim: It was previously reported that spindle orientation is indicative of whether an ISC mitosis is asymmetric or symmetric.
source: It was previously reported that spindle orientation is indicative of whether an ISC mitosis is asymmetric or symmetric, with symmetric divisions being planar relative to the visceral muscle layer, and asymmetric divisions displacing one daughter cell apically, away from the visceral muscle (Hu and Jasper, 2019; Ohlstein and Spradling, 2007; Goulas et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Measured angles between sister cells after mitosis were found to be <15° in 29/33 cases for RasG12V- and in 30/32 cases for stg +CycE-induced mitoses.

claim: No significant difference in cell motility was found when directly comparing both pair types irrespective of genotype or time-point analyzed.

claim: Cells of both pair types migrate within the epithelium at similar speeds.
